title: Five Nights at Freddy's
notes: Plays, slower on macOS 27. On macOS 26.6.2 the menu and a night ran at a steady 60 fps on DXVK, GPU about 0.5 ms, on an Apple M1 Pro (engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r2). On macOS 27.0 the office, where the nights are spent, runs at about 18 to 27 fps whatever the graphics mode: 18 on DXVK (MoltenVK's own count, no screen capture running) and 25 on Wine's own Direct3D on an M4 with engine r15, 27 on DXVK with the Wine 11 engine, and about 16 on the M1 Pro. The menu stays fast. The game's own work is the slow part, with one to two CPU cores busy, so no graphics mode, engine or sync setting changes it; a change in Rosetta on macOS 27 is the likely cause, not confirmed. It is still playable. It is a Clickteam Fusion Direct3D 9 game, so DXVK (the automatic and DXVK modes both route Direct3D 9 through it) stays the mode. A save is written under the environment, so Continue works on the next launch. On a display that is not 16:10 apply the recipe: it sets EmulateModeset for the game so Wine emulates the 1280x800 mode the game asks for and the picture fills the screen instead of landing off centre (highball#72). That setting does not change the frame rate. Re-checked on 2026-10-05 on an M4 with engine r21 (DEP kept on): the main menu comes up on DXVK as before. A player's numbers put the start of the slowdown between macOS 26.6 and 26.7: 21 fps in the office on 26.7 and 20 on 27, against 60 before (highball#400, 2026-10-22).

verified.fps: main menu reached, not played this run
verified.how: Steam copy through Highball on an M4 on 2026-10-05, DXVK, engine r21: main menu at 100 s.

knownIssues.symptom: The office runs at about 18 to 27 fps on macOS 27, where it ran at 60 on macOS 26, and already on macOS 26.7 (21 fps there, highball#400)
knownIssues.cause: Not the graphics mode, the engine, the sync mode or the display setting: all measured the same on an M4 with macOS 27.0 on 2026-09-30. The frame waits about 50 ms on something the game does, with one to two CPU cores busy. Rosetta's slow x87 maths is not what holds it: with the x87 accelerator (athei's x87sidecar 1.7.0 on the Wine 11 engine, highball#165) the CPU use halved but the office stayed at 19 to 21 fps against 22 without it

knownIssues.symptom: Without the recipe, on a display whose logical resolution is not 16:10: the picture sits down and to the right with black bars along the top and left, and is clipped at the right and bottom edges.
knownIssues.cause: The game asks Wine for a 1280x800 fullscreen mode; Wine's Mac driver reports success but leaves the display as it is (measured 2026-09-07), so the game positions itself for a resolution it never got.
knownIssues.fix: The recipe (2026-09-11): one registry value, EmulateModeset=y for the game's executable, makes Wine emulate the mode change and scale the fullscreen window to the real screen. Verified by eye at 1728x1117: fills the screen, centred. No engine change, works on the default engine.

knownIssues.symptom: On a 14-inch M1 Pro the game draws small in a corner of the screen and the mouse position does not match what it clicks (reported on 0.9.12, highball#67)
knownIssues.cause: not established. The reporter has the recipe's display-mode setting applied, the same one that centred the picture at 1728x1117 here on 2026-09-11, so something else differs on their Mac.
knownIssues.fix: none confirmed. highball#72, which this pointed to, closed with the recipe, but this report comes after it. To be retested here on the current engine: a first look on 2026-09-24, with the session locked and nothing visible, found the window centred at about 90 percent of the screen rather than filling it, which settles nothing.

knownIssues.symptom: On the Wine 11 engines (x64-crossover26.3-r11, r12) under DXVK the game runs at about 40 fps with cut sound and uneven frames, against 76 fps on the default engine's DXVK Direct3D 9 (Metal HUD, menu, M1 Pro, macOS 27.0, 2026-09-25).
knownIssues.cause: DXVK's Direct3D 9 is slower on that tree, GPU time is under a millisecond either way. Separately, an environment where the Sims recipe was applied carries MVK_SHADOW_IMPORT=1 bottle-wide, and on those engines that stops DXVK's Direct3D 9 from drawing at all (highball#198).
knownIssues.fix: stay on the default engine for this game, or on a Wine 11 engine use Wine's own Direct3D. From Highball 0.9.38 the DXMT and D3DMetal modes do that on their own on r11 and r12 (the engine says so); the DXVK mode, which this row recommends for the default engine, still uses DXVK's Direct3D 9 everywhere.
